question: A constant force F acts on a box of mass 10 kg for a duration of 2 s. It increases the object's velocity from 6 m/s to 10 m/s. The magnitude of the applied force F is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**20 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The change in velocity (Δv) of the box is given by the difference between the final velocity and the initial velocity, which is 10 m/s - 6 m/s = 4 m/s.
 
• The time duration (t) during which the force acts is 2 seconds.
 
• Using the formula for acceleration (a) a = Δv / t, we get a = 4 m/s / 2 s = 2 m/s².
 
• According to Newton's second law of motion, Force (F) is given by F = m * a, where m is the mass of the object.
 
• Substituting the values, F = 10 kg * 2 m/s² = 20 N.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:**

 
 
• This law states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of that object times its acceleration (F = m * a).
 
• It explains how the velocity of an object changes when it is subjected to an external force.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration (a):**
 
 
• It is the rate of change of velocity of an object.
 
• It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
 
 
• **Force (F):**
 
 
• A push or pull acting upon an object as a result of its interaction with another object.
 
• Measured in Newtons (N) in the International System of Units (SI).
 
 
 
• **Velocity (v):**
 
 
• The speed of something in a given direction.
 
• It is also a vector quantity, meaning it includes both speed and direction.
